name: Houses That Held the Thrones
description: From the emperors of Rome and the Han to the Habsburgs and the Windsors: the families that ran states for centuries and what brought each one down.

checkpoints.name: Ancient lines
checkpoints.note: The first great dynasties set the pattern. Qin united China, the Han made its government last, Rome's Julio-Claudians ruled as emperors, and the Ptolemies governed Egypt as heirs of Alexander.

checkpoints.name: Dynasties of the middle ages
checkpoints.note: In China the Tang held a golden age, while in western Europe the Carolingians built an empire under Charlemagne. Families, not states, held lands together.

checkpoints.name: Houses at their height
checkpoints.note: The Habsburgs rose in central Europe, the Plantagenets ruled England and half of France, and the Mongol Yuan, then the Ming, held China. The Ottomans began as one family among many in Anatolia.

checkpoints.name: Crowns of the early modern world
checkpoints.note: Tudors ruled England, then Stuarts and Hanoverians ruled Britain, Safavids ruled Persia, the Romanovs took Russia, and the Manchu Qing conquered China and ruled it from Beijing. Wars and revolutions tested each of them.

checkpoints.name: The last royal houses
checkpoints.note: The age of republics ended many dynasties: the Qing, Habsburgs, Romanovs and Ottomans fell, and the Pahlavis in Iran. The Windsors and the House of Saud remain.
